newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria H1 group operating profit up 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria H1 group operating profit up 25 pct.

text.p: Bank Austria, presenting its first fully consolidated earnings since taking over rival Creditanstalt, reported a 25 percent jump in first half group operating profit on Monday.
Bank Austria preferred shares were two schillings (15 cents) up at 440 in pre-market activity. Creditanstalt preferred were 0.2 schillings down at 565.

In a statement released ahead of a news conference, Bank Austria said group operating profit reached 7.12 billion schillings in the six months to the end of June, up from 5.67 billion the previous year.

Creditanstalt had flagged improved group earnings on Friday when it announced a 70 percent surge in first half net profit. Its operating result rose 38 percent to 4.2 billion schillings, setting the pace for the rest of the group.
Bank Austria operating income climbed to 21.5 billion schillings from 19.02 billion. Operating expenses stood at 14.38 billion schillings after 13.35 billion.

Net interest income was flat at 11.69 billion schillings, compared with 11.66 billion the previous year. Commission income rose to 4.33 billion schillings from 3.91 billion. The group's trading result rose to 2.73 billion from 1.55 billion.
Personnel expenses increased to 8.2 billion schillings from 7.64 billion. ($ = 12.96 Austrian Schillings)
